tools.name: sfizz / sfizz-ui
tools.role: sfizz is the SFZ parser/sample-synthesis library and JACK client. sfizz-ui supplies instrument plugins including VST3; neither is a DAW or a complete recorded instrument collection.
tools.windows: Official downloads list Windows 7+ 32/64-bit installers. Match the VST3 architecture to the Windows host; AU is macOS-specific.
tools.license: BSD-2-Clause for both repositories; samples and third-party dependencies have separate terms.
tools.maintenance: Both GitHub repositories explicitly show archived/read-only since 2026-06-21. Latest release links resolve to 1.2.3.
tools.source_requirement: Supply a licensed SFZ and its referenced recordings. Official documentation states SFZv1 and partial SFZv2 support; verify required opcodes/articulations.
tools.recommendation: Conditional fixed-version SFZ candidate after host and instrument tests; do not describe the archived upstream as an actively maintained default.

tools.name: FluidSynth
tools.role: SoundFont MIDI synthesizer with command-line offline/fast rendering and C API. It includes reverb/chorus but is not a VST3 host; SFZ is not its native format.
tools.windows: Official download page provides automatically built Windows binary releases; its CLI does not require Python.
tools.license: LGPL; repository LICENSE contains version 2.1. The official FAQ permits commercial music while requiring checks of MIDI and SoundFont input licenses. Bundling/linking software is a separate question.
tools.maintenance: Recent release fixes note-onset, MIDI, reverb and DSP issues; official news also lists 2.6.1 on 2026-09-19 and 2.6.0 on 2026-08-11.
tools.source_requirement: Official SoundFont documentation explicitly requires an external SoundFont. Generic GM bank availability does not establish authentic ethnic-instrument quality or rights.
tools.stem_plan: Render each isolated instrument/channel MIDI to a stem, or explicitly configure the documented multichannel API. Default stereo rendering is not automatic stem separation. Make chorus/reverb settings explicit.
tools.recommendation: First lightweight MIDI renderer candidate when an appropriate licensed SF2/SF3 bank already exists; do not blindly convert SFZ or substitute generic GM timbres for authentic instruments.

tools.name: DawDreamer
tools.role: Python processor graphs with MIDI, plugin instruments/effects, automation, state saving/loading and simultaneous processor recording. Official example saves dry instrument output and wet graph output.
tools.windows: Windows x86-64 Python 3.11–3.14; current PyPI metadata includes dawdreamer-0.9.0-cp313-cp313-win_amd64.whl, matching the reported local Python 3.13 architecture family.
tools.license: GPL-3.0; hosted plugins, samples and third-party dependencies retain separate terms.
tools.maintenance: Release adds rendering/concurrency and platform-wheel changes; current repository shows 12 commits since release. Documentation header is 0.9.1, ahead of released 0.9.0; pin APIs to the installed release.
tools.source_requirement: The desired recorded instruments require supplied sample audio or external plugins/sample libraries; the framework is not a guzheng/dizi/string recording collection.
tools.recommendation: Preferred candidate for Python-controlled multitrack graphs when independent stems, automation, presets and return effects are central. Begin with one known instrument and test timing/state/tails.

tools.name: Pedalboard
tools.role: Python audio I/O and effects, plus Windows VST3 instrument/effect hosting. MIDI-to-instrument rendering exists since 0.7.4: describing it as effects-only is incorrect.
tools.windows: Windows amd64 wheels and automated VST tests; current release has Python 3.10–3.15 wheels, including pedalboard-0.9.26-cp313-cp313-win_amd64.whl.
tools.license: GPL-3.0; README lists statically included third-party libraries separately. External instruments and samples are not relicensed by the host.
tools.maintenance: Current release fixes Linux wheel CPU compatibility; current documentation, Windows wheels and Windows VST test claims are present.
tools.source_requirement: Built-in effects process supplied audio. Recorded-instrument MIDI rendering requires a separately supplied compatible VST3 instrument and authorized sample library.
tools.state_and_tail_caveat: Successive chunks of the same stream need reset=False to preserve internal state. Render duration must include releases/tails; MIDI timestamps outside it are ignored. Per-part dry stems and routing remain application responsibilities.
tools.recommendation: Preferred lightweight addition for processing existing stems; also viable for simple per-part MIDI/VST3 rendering. DawDreamer's processor graph/recording model is more explicit for complex routing.

skill_routing_recommendations: Licensed SF2/SF3 plus MIDI: evaluate FluidSynth; export aligned per-instrument dry stems.
Licensed VST3 plus score/automation: evaluate DawDreamer; Pedalboard is an alternative for simple per-part renders.
Existing dry WAV stems: evaluate Pedalboard for parameterized effects/shared returns; retain originals.
Licensed SFZ multisamples: sfizz-ui remains conditional, pinned and archived; validate required opcodes and the chosen host.
Record score/MIDI, tempo, note durations, velocities, CC/articulations and explicit sample mappings.
Record engine/plugin versions, architecture, presets/state, sample hashes and separate license evidence.
Record sample rate, block size, dry/wet routing and tail allowance; verify a repeated short render before full export.
Keep numerical/source checks separate from listening. Better tools do not establish natural timbre or repair poor source recordings.
runtime_status: None of these tools was installed, imported or rendered in this research. Published wheels and documentation are capability evidence, not local runtime acceptance.
date_method: Release timestamps were read from public GitHub HTML relative-time datetime attributes. Latest links and PyPI JSON corroborated tags; no GitHub API retry was used.
